input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
input.rationale:
On re-examination there is a genuine parametric shortfall, not merely the formatting false negative I reported twice before. The preferred position requires twelve months of conformity for SOFTWARE and ninety days for services. The document's definitions split software into two tracks and only one is adequately warranted:

(1) Section 1.7 defines "Services" as the HOSTED software plus implementation and related services. Hosted software is fully covered: Section 19.2 warrants Hosted Services conformity "throughout the subscription term", which meets or exceeds the twelve-month software benchmark.

(2) Section 13.2, however, expressly contemplates "software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable", granting us a perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence. That software is not hosted, so the full-term Hosted Services warranty does not reach it. Section 1.4 defines "Deliverable" as reports, configurations, integrations, specifications, designs, workflows and training materials and expressly EXCLUDES Vendor Technology. So perpetually licensed software reaches the conformity warranty only when embedded in a Deliverable, and then only for ninety days — the fallback level, not the preferred twelve months. Standalone paid-up Vendor Technology arguably carries no durational conformity period at all.

REDLINE: a single minimal amendment to Section 19.2 extends the period to twelve (12) months for any Deliverable that consists of or embeds software or Vendor Technology licensed on a paid-up or perpetual basis, leaving ninety days for all other (services-type) Deliverables. This also renders the period in numerals, which resolves the deterministic period check that failed on the spelled-out "ninety days". Fallback: ninety days across the board if Vendor confirms software is always delivered hosted.

ALL OTHER ELEMENTS REMAIN COMPLIANT and are untouched: 19.1 professional/workmanlike plus material conformity; 19.3 malicious code and Applicable Law; 19.4 re-perform/repair/replace with termination-and-refund backstop, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; 19.5 disclaims implied warranties only and preserves express warranties, so no carve-out edit is needed. The ninety-day clock also runs from the later of delivery or acceptance, which is better than the delivery-only benchmark. Separately noted: the 19.3 malicious-code warranty covers only code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", narrower than a flat no-malicious-code warranty; left unflagged as standard market language given the non-exclusive remedy and security obligations carried as Excluded Claims under 21.3.

proposal.summary: Extend the Deliverable conformity period to twelve (12) months for Deliverables consisting of or embedding perpetually/paid-up licensed software or Vendor Technology; keep ninety (90) days for other Deliverables and add numerals.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 19.2 warrants Hosted Services for the full subscription term, but software and Vendor Technology licensed to us on a paid-up or perpetual basis under Section 13.2 is not hosted and so receives only the ninety-day Deliverable period. Our position is twelve months of conformity for software, so we have extended the period for software Deliverables while leaving ninety days for all other Deliverables; we can accept ninety days across the board as a fallback if the software is in practice always delivered hosted.

ops.oldText: For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria.
ops.newText: For ninety (90) days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria, provided that for any Deliverable that consists of or embeds software or Vendor Technology licensed to Customer on a paid-up or perpetual basis, that period is twelve (12) months.
